abstract: Unlike fractional quantum Hall states in uniform Landau levels, fractional Chern insulators can host dispersive anyon bands, raising the question of what happens when the anyon gap closes. We construct an exact finite-bond-dimension tensor-network state for a fractional Chern semimetal by Gutzwiller projecting a critical parton state. This state exhibits divergent correlation lengths in charged sectors but a fractionally quantized many-body Chern number of $1/3$. Although it has one electron per unit cell, its modular $S$ and $T$ matrices and entanglement spectrum match those of the $ν=1/3$ Laughlin state. We identify a $(1+1)$--dimensional $U(3)_1\times SU(3)_1$ conformal field theory (CFT) governing the wavefunction norm in the infrared, an unexpected result for a state with $U(1)_3$ topology. The $SU(3)_1$ sector is a nonlinear sigma model whose Wess--Zumino level and kinetic stiffness are determined by the parton Chern number and Fubini--Study metric, respectively. Under renormalization, it flows to the conformal fixed point, with an initial distance to this fixed point controlled by the idealness of parton quantum geometry. Favorable geometry enables precise agreement with CFT predictions even on narrow cylinders.
